The cloak has a circular-elliptical shaped boundary.
The general coordinate transformation method is used to design the cloak.
The cloak can channel incident waves smoothly around objects.
The PEC object has dimensions al = 0.2 m, hI = 0.1 m and CI = 0.3 m.
The frequency of the incident wave is 3 GHz.
The angle of incidence in Fig. 2(c) is 40° with respect to the x-axis.
The axial-ratio of the cloak in Fig. 2(d) is al = 0.1 m, hI = 0.4 m and CI = 0.5 m.
The material property in the z-direction is uniform.
The shape of the inner boundary is elliptical.
The shape of the outer boundary is circular.
The Jacobian transformation tensor is a matrix that relates the original and transformed coordinates.
The anisotropic property of the transformed materials is defined by Eqs. (3) - (8) in the paper.
The perfectly matched layer (PML) boundaries are used to remove undesired numerical reflections in the simulation.
The software used for the full-wave simulations is COMSOL Multiphysics.
The simulation results show that the cloak works well for different angles of incidence and shielded object dimensions.
The cloak can be designed with different axial-ratios and still channel incident waves smoothly around objects.
